raw_response:
*[sits down, lights a cigarette, thinks out loud]*

Alright, let me tell you how I'm going about things this year. I've worked these 11.6 mu for sixty years — since I was a boy following my father. My wife and me, we do everything ourselves now. The kids went to the city long ago, they send money sometimes but they don't come back to help with the fields.

Eleven mu is too much for two old people really, but it's what we have. I keep it split up so if one thing goes bad, the others carry us. My father did it that way, I do it the same.

**The maize** — spring maize, about 4-and-a-half mu on the better ground near the house. I plant after Qingming when the soil warms up, maybe around April 20 or so, depends on the weather. I buy hybrid seed from the shop in town, the same kind as last year because it did okay — about 30 yuan per mu of seed. Before plowing I put down two bags of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, that's the blue bag. Then when the maize is knee-high I go through and drop a handful of urea by each plant — probably one bag of urea for the whole patch. I don't measure it exact, my hand knows. I water maybe twice from the well if the sky doesn't help, water costs money these days with the meter. Last year I got something like 450 kilos per mu, this year if the rain comes right I hope for the same.

**The cotton** — 3 mu on the sandy piece. Cotton is hard on an old man, all the picking, all the spraying. But the price is better than grain and that patch doesn't grow maize well anyway. I plant in late April when it's warm enough, use the seed I get from the co-op. I don't put too much fertilizer on cotton — if you give it too much nitrogen the plant grows tall and leafy and the bolls don't set. One bag of compound at planting and maybe a little urea when it's flowering. The big cost is spray — bollworm, aphids, every two weeks sometimes I have to go out with the backpack sprayer. My nephew comes to help with picking in September, I pay him something or give him grain.

**The peanut** — 3 mu, on lighter soil. Peanut is easy for fertilizer, it makes its own nitrogen from the roots, everyone knows that. I just put down some compound and phosphate before planting. The trouble with peanut is pulling them at harvest — it's hard on the back. We dig them in October, spread them out to dry on the threshing floor. Peanut price is decent, and the oil mill in town buys them.

**The mungbean** — just 1 mu on the corner piece that doesn't do well for anything else. Mungbean doesn't need much of anything. I throw the seed in after the spring rain in May, it grows on its own. Maybe one pass of weeding. Mungbean for the household to eat and a little to sell. Old people's crop.

For spraying and fertilizer and seed all together, maybe 2,500-3,000 yuan for everything this year. That's most of what we have. Water from the well maybe 400 yuan on top. If the weather is bad we eat the loss, there's nothing to do.

decision.reasoning_summary: I do things the way I've always done them, the way my father taught me. Four crops on eleven mu keeps us safe — if cotton prices drop we still have grain, if the rain misses the maize the peanut still carries on. I don't buy more fertilizer than I can pay for, and I don't change the varieties unless a neighbor has shown me something really works. My wife and I can handle most of it ourselves, but for cotton picking I'll need my nephew to come for a few days. An old farmer with two old hands has to be careful — we keep some cash aside for the water meter and in case the sprayer breaks.
